bull.b: Revenue grew 93% year over year in Q2, while raised 2026 guidance points to 82% growth at the midpoint. This acceleration, reinforced by record deal activity and customer conversions, indicates broadening platform adoption and supports durable expansion over the next several quarters.

Exceptional operating margins and free cash flow provide substantial internal funding for product investment, hiring, and customer expansion. Cash generation closely tracking earnings also supports strong earnings quality, while the sizeable liquid balance strengthens resilience and strategic flexibility.

A 157% net dollar retention rate shows existing customers are expanding their Palantir deployments, creating recurring growth beyond new-account wins. Rising customer counts and multiple pilots converting into multi-year contracts suggest the platforms can become embedded in operational workflows.

bear.t: U.S. revenue concentration and international lag
bear.b: Heavy dependence on the U.S. exposes growth to the spending priorities and procurement cycles of one geographic market. International commercial growth is materially slower, limiting diversification and making sustained expansion more dependent on continued U.S. government and commercial momentum.

Recent profitability has improved sharply from losses to exceptionally high margins, but those levels may be difficult to maintain if operating conditions normalize. Any margin moderation could reduce the pace of earnings compounding and constrain the cash available for reinvestment.

bear.t: Large-deal concentration may increase revenue volatility
bear.b: Large contract wins can accelerate growth, but greater dependence on sizeable bookings makes reported revenue more sensitive to contract timing, scope changes, or termination. This concentration can produce less predictable growth than a broader base of smaller, recurring commitments.
